subject: Crescent Consulting — Connector validation & reference design kickoff
messages:
From: Dinesh Singh <d.singh@crescentconsult.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Crescent connector validation & reference design kickoff

Hi Kimberly / Marissa,

Thanks again for agreeing to run the partner connector validation for Crescent. We finished the first-pass reference design yesterday and want to kickoff technical validation next week. High-level asks: confirm staging access, agree on a test matrix (smoke / canary / scale), and validate fallback behavior when Redwood Dedicated falls back to hosted variants.

Attached: crescent-reference-design-v1.pdf and an initial connector-test-matrix spreadsheet.

Proposed kickoff: Thu 2027-09-09 10:00PT. Would love a short agenda (30-45m) and who from your side should join (engineering + partner ops).

A few notes from our side:
- We plan to exercise prefix caching + quantized model path; recommend running 10k short-chat tokens and a 1k-long-seq batch for throughput.
- We will need a short-lived staging key (scoped) and an SSH tunnel to your staging collector for logs.

Can you confirm the time and whether Redwood can perform a controlled failover test during the session?

Thanks,
Dinesh
Partner Engineering
Crescent Consulting

---
Attachments: crescent-reference-design-v1.pdf (pdf), connector-test-matrix-20270907.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Dinesh Singh <d.singh@crescentconsult.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Crescent connector validation & reference design kickoff

Dinesh —

Appreciate the quick turnaround on the reference material. Thu 09/09 10:00PT works for us; I will book a 45m slot and invite service reliability and partner ops. Agenda suggestion: 1) goals & success criteria (10m), 2) staging access + test matrix review (10m), 3) live smoke and failover demo plan (20m), 4) next steps + roll-forward schedule (5m).

Two asks before the call:
- Can you share the staging key TTL and IP allowlist for the tunnel? We prefer short-lived keys (24h) scoped to test routes.
- Please flag any non-standard model variants that need explicit kernel pins — that will determine whether we run on Dedicated pools or fallback to hosted.

I'll assign Sergio to own the technical runbook during validation. Marissa, can you cover partner coordination and the procurement checklist (if we need any capacity reservation)?

Thanks — see calendar invite; joining details included.

Kimberly Park
Head of Partnerships — Technical Alliances
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

---
Note: calendar invite created (Redwood Conference Room / Zoom).
From: Dinesh Singh <d.singh@crescentconsult.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Crescent connector validation & reference design kickoff

Kimberly / team —

Quick update ahead of the call: attaching an updated test matrix with explicit pass/fail criteria and test-data buckets. Also added a short step-by-step for provisioning the scoped staging key (staging-access-instructions.txt). We set the default TTL to 24 hours and will provide an allowlist for the Redwood egress IPs; see the attachment.

Important: there are two optional extended tests in the matrix: 1) slow-network simulation (packet loss + 200ms latency), and 2) model-variant quantization parity checks. We recommend running both during the canary window but can skip for the smoke run.

Forwarding the relevant section from our internal runbook for visibility:

> On Wed, Sep 1, 2027, Crescent Integration Team wrote:
>
> 1) Create a scoped staging API key with only /v1/stream and /v1/embeddings permissions.
> 2) Configure collector endpoint to accept compressed NDJSON and rotate logs every 15m.
> 3) For controlled failover, trigger the dedicated->hosted route via header: X-Redwood-Fallback: force_hosted.

We will join the call with an engineer (Anjali Rao) who will drive the demo. See attached files.

Best,
Dinesh
Crescent Consulting

---
Attachments: connector-test-matrix-20270907.xlsx, staging-access-instructions.txt
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Dinesh Singh <d.singh@crescentconsult.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2027 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Crescent connector validation & reference design kickoff (post-call)

Dinesh —

Good session today; thank you to you and Anjali for the demos. Quick recap and action items:

Recap: we validated the reference connector in staging, executed the smoke tests (latency, prefix caching, short-chat token paths) and a controlled failover using the X-Redwood-Fallback header. We observed expected degradation in latency when routing to hosted (median increase ~180ms) but no correctness regressions in the API responses.

Action items:
- Crescent: upload final reference design with sequence diagrams to the shared Drive folder (you said you would) — due 2027-09-13.
- Crescent: provide the final allowlist IP file for production egress so we can arrange Dedicated reservations if needed — due 2027-09-14.
- Redwood (Sergio): draft a short runbook for canary rollout (steps, rollback triggers, monitoring checks) and attach to PARTNER-1342 — due 2027-09-10 COB.
- Kimberly / Marissa: review procurement notes and confirm whether we need a one-off capacity reservation for the canary window.

Attachments from our side: redwood-canary-runbook-template.md (attached here for Sergio to start from).

If everything looks good, let's target a canary window the week of 2027-09-20.

Thanks again — I will follow up with the runbook PR.

Kimberly Park
Head of Partnerships — Technical Alliances
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
